text:
### Observed differences

- Before, A27 ran in about 52 in 100 cases (roughly once per case when present); in the later window it runs in about 199 of 200 cases, about once per case. [OCC001]
- Before, A32, A33 and A38 each ran in about 48–49 in 100 cases; in the later window each appears in only about 1 of 200 cases. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- Before, the outgoing transitions of A26 split between A27 (about 51%), A38 (about 18%), A33 (about 16%) and A32 (about 14%); in the later window about 97 in 100 of them go to A27. [DIR001]
- Before, A27 and each of A32, A33, A38 were mutually exclusive alternatives (A27 alone in about 51 in 100 cases, the other activity alone in about 48–49 in 100, essentially never together); in the later window only A27 remains. [REL006, REL007, REL008]
- Before, when the branch was taken, A32, A33 and A38 all occurred in the same case (about 48–49 in 100 cases), appeared in both orders between them (no fixed order), and each preceded A28; in the later window they no longer co-occur. [REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- Before, A26 reached A28 at a distance of 2 steps in about half the cases and 4 steps in about 47 in 100; in the later window the distance is 2 steps in about 97 in 100 cases. [LAG001]
- The retained edge A27 → A28 is essentially unchanged: about 97% of A27's outgoing transitions before and about 99% after, at distance 1 in both windows. [DIR002, LAG004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the branch between A26 and A28 running through A32, A33 and A38 — executed in about half of the earlier cases, with the three activities in varying internal order before reaching A28 — is no longer executed in the later window, and that virtually all cases now run A26 → A27 → A28. This rests on direct, mutually consistent participation, routing, relational and distance evidence: the three branch activities fall from about 97–98 of 200 traces to 1 of 200, A26's outgoing transitions concentrate on A27 (about 51% to about 97%), A26–A27 and A27–A28 co-occurrence rises to near certainty while co-occurrence with the branch activities collapses, and the A26→A28 distance collapses from a 2-step/4-step mix to almost always 2 steps. The screening count (31 qualifying items against roughly 0.57 expected without change) is far above what an unchanged process would produce, and the per-activity sample sizes (about 97–98 traces before versus 1 after, out of 200 in each window) make a rare-variant sampling explanation implausible. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR001, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL009, LAG001, LAG004]

Limitations: zero participation in the later window only means the branch was not observed there, so the evidence cannot distinguish a branch that was removed from one that remains possible but was skipped in every observed case. The items describing the branch's internal routing in the later window (for example A32's or A38's outgoing transitions) each rest on a single after-window trace and add no reliable support. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the branch still exists but is triggered only by case types absent from the later sample. [DIR003, DIR004, LAG002, LAG003, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

Other differences: in the later window, A26 and A27 each show a few new outgoing transitions that occur in about 1 trace apiece (each well under 1% of that activity's outgoing transitions). [DIR001, DIR002]
